title: Speed of Sound in a Gas - Sea Level Air
learningObjectives: Understand that speed of sound in an ideal gas follows a = sqrt(gamma R T) and rises with absolute temperature and depends on gamma and R.
Interpret Mach number as the ratio of flow speed to local sound speed and use it to judge when compressibility effects become important.
Describe the isentropic density-velocity relation drho/rho = -M^2 dV/V and how its magnitude grows with Mach number.

explanations.text: The speed of sound is the speed at which small isentropic pressure disturbances propagate, and the Mach number compares any gas or aircraft speed to that sound speed to indicate flow regime.

evidence.quote: The speed of sound is equal to the speed of transmission of small, isentropic disturbances in the flow.
The Mach number is the ratio of the speed of the aircraft, or the speed of the gas, to the speed of sound in the gas.

explanations.text: For an ideal gas the sound speed is set by gamma, the specific gas constant R and absolute temperature T through the identity gamma R T = a squared derived from p = rho R T.
Near sea level the sound speed is about 330 m/s. Well below it density changes are small, while near and above it density changes scale with Mach number squared and compressibility cannot be ignored.

evidence.quote: Near and beyond the speed of sound, about 330 m/s or 760 mph at sea level
